title: Skill requirement to reveal a mission
text: A mission can be revealed only if the leaders assigned to it together have at least as many matching skill icons as its skill requirement. Otherwise it stays facedown and the player must activate a system, reveal another mission or pass. This also applies to leaders assigned by abilities.

title: Revealing a mission
text: Steps: 1 flip the card and read it; 2 choose a legal system and place the assigned leaders there; 3 an "attempt" can be opposed, a "resolve" cannot; 4 the opponent may send one leader from his pool to oppose; 5 if opposed, roll dice; 6 on success apply the ability; 7 a starting mission returns to hand, any other mission is discarded.

title: Unopposed missions succeed
text: If the opponent has no leader in the mission's system, an attempted mission succeeds automatically.

title: Opposed missions
text: With leaders of both sides in the system, each player rolls one die per matching skill icon on all his leaders there (any colour, at most 10 dice), current player first. The attempt succeeds only with more successes than the opponent. A matching leader portrait on the card adds two successes. An opponent leader without matching icons still forces a roll needing at least one success.

title: Missions attempted against a leader
text: A mission "against a leader" is attempted in that leader's system and that leader always takes part, even if it is captured; all leaders in the system participate. A leader sent to oppose does not change the target.

title: Leader removed from a mission card
text: If a leader on a mission card is eliminated, captured or moved off the mission, the card returns to its owner's hand unrevealed.

title: Missions on the Rebel Base space
text: If a mission is attempted or resolved on the "Rebel Base" space, the leader is put on that space, not in the system where the base is hidden.

title: Starting missions
text: Each faction has four starting missions (marked by an arrow) in hand from the start. They return to hand after use and can never be discarded.

title: Project cards
text: The project deck holds Imperial mission cards that the Empire draws with its Research and Development mission. Discarded projects go to the project discard pile.

title: Missions without benefit; attempt versus resolve
text: A mission may be revealed and resolved even if it gives no or only partial benefit. Only attempted missions can succeed or fail; resolved missions neither succeed nor fail.

title: Errata to three base game cards
text: The FAQ corrects where the Rebel missions Sabotage (any populous system) and Covert Operation (any system with at least one Imperial unit) are attempted, and forbids the Imperial action card Independent Operation from moving units into a system with Rebel ground units.

title: Action cards
text: Action cards recruit leaders and give one-use abilities; a used card is revealed, resolved and returned to the box. The heading says when it can be used (Assignment, Start of Combat, Immediate, Special). In a mission or combat it needs one of its leaders already in that system. Use is optional; own cards may be checked anytime, the opponent's are hidden; on a tie the current player goes first.

title: Objective cards
text: The Rebels start with one objective and draw one each Refresh. An objective is played when its requirement is met at its stated time (Combat, Start of Refresh Phase, ...) and gives the reputation shown, then leaves the game. At most one is played per combat and per Refresh Phase. Objectives are hidden, have no hand limit, and the deck is stacked stage I over II over III.

title: Objective timing and open card backs
text: An objective must be played as soon as its requirement is fulfilled; one that needs a won battle is played at the end of the combat; after one objective in a combat no other (not even Death Star Plans) can be played there. The combat is initiated by the player whose turn it is, otherwise by the player whose card caused it. Objective card backs are open information.

title: Probe cards
text: The probe deck has one card for every system except Coruscant. It sets starting loyalty during setup and the Rebels secretly take their base card from it. Each Refresh the Empire draws two probe cards and keeps them hidden from the Rebels.

title: Tactic cards
text: Tactic cards are drawn in combat according to leaders' tactic values, plus one for each special result spent. They stay hidden until played, and at the end of each combat all space and ground tactic cards are shuffled back into their decks.

title: The Death Star
text: The Death Star follows the rules for ships except that it has no health and cannot be damaged, and while a Death Star or Death Star Under Construction is in a combat the Empire cannot retreat any units. Both are space stations, not capital ships or structures.

title: Building a second Death Star
text: The Construct Death Star project places an immobile Death Star Under Construction in the mission's system and a Death Star on space 3 of the build queue. The new Death Star can only be deployed in that system. If the unfinished station is destroyed, the queued Death Star is destroyed too.

title: Destroying a Death Star
text: In a space battle, after both attacks, the Rebels may reveal a Death Star Plans objective. With at least one fighter in the system they roll three dice; any direct hit destroys the Death Star and gives the card's reputation, otherwise the card is kept. One such card per combat round; it also works on the unfinished station but needs a Death Star in the system.

title: Death Star Under Construction rulings
text: Cards that name the Death Star do not work for the Death Star Under Construction unless they say so. The finished Death Star is placed in the unfinished station's system even if Rebel ground units are there. Destroying the unfinished station without Death Star Plans gives no reputation.

title: Destroying systems with the Death Star
text: To destroy a system the Empire needs the Superlaser Online project, drawn through Research and Development. The destroyed system gets a marker and loses all Rebel ground units. If it is the system of the Rebel base, the Empire wins immediately.
